whatIsFlattening.question: What does flattening a PDF mean?
whatIsFlattening.answer: Flattening merges interactive form fields — text boxes, checkboxes, dropdowns, radio buttons — into the page content itself. The answers stay visible, but the fields are gone, so nobody can edit them anymore.

whenToFlatten.question: When should I flatten a PDF form?
whenToFlatten.answer: Flatten after you've filled a form and before you submit, email, or print it. It locks your answers in place and ensures the form looks the same in every PDF viewer. You can fill forms first with our Fill Form tool, then flatten the result here.

reversible.question: Can flattening be undone?
reversible.answer: No — flattening is permanent in the output file. The original file on your device is never modified, though, so keep it if you may need to edit the form again later.

noFields.question: Why does it say my PDF has no form fields?
noFields.answer: Only PDFs with interactive (AcroForm) fields can be flattened. If your form is a scanned image or plain text with underscores, there is nothing interactive to lock — the document is already non-editable in that sense.

privacy.question: Is my file uploaded to a server?
privacy.answer: No. This tool runs 100% in your browser — the PDF is read, flattened, and saved on your own device. Your file never leaves your computer.

whichFormField.question: Which form field types can be flattened?
whichFormField.answer: All standard interactive (AcroForm) fields: text boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons, and dropdown lists. The tool lists every detected field by name before flattening, so you can see exactly what will be merged into the page.

fillFormFlattening.question: Can I fill a form before flattening it?
fillFormFlattening.answer: Yes — that's the intended workflow. Use the BlendPDF Fill Form tool to type your answers into the interactive fields, download the filled PDF, then flatten it here so the answers can't be changed.

flattenPasswordProtected.question: Can I flatten password-protected PDFs?
flattenPasswordProtected.answer: Not directly — encrypted PDFs can't be modified without the password. Remove the password first with the BlendPDF Unlock PDF tool, then flatten the unlocked file.

fileSizeLimits.question: What are the file size limits?
fileSizeLimits.answer: PDF files up to 50MB are supported, with no page limit. Since flattening runs locally in your browser, speed depends on your device rather than any server.

originalFileModified.question: Is my original file modified?
originalFileModified.answer: No. The flattened document is saved as a new file prefixed with "flattened-", and your original — with its editable fields — stays untouched on your device.

flattenPdfsMobile.question: Can I flatten PDFs on mobile devices?
flattenPdfsMobile.answer: Yes, the tool works on smartphones and tablets. You can review the detected field list, flatten, and download the locked copy directly from your mobile browser.

flatteningPdfsFree.question: Is flattening PDFs free?
flatteningPdfsFree.answer: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Files up to 50MB are supported, and you can flatten as many forms as you need.

flatteningArabicPdf.question: Does flattening work with Arabic PDF forms?
flatteningArabicPdf.answer: Yes. Flattening merges each field's rendered appearance into the page, so Arabic answers and RTL layouts are preserved as displayed. BlendPDF is built Arabic-first, and the rest of the document's Arabic text is untouched by flattening.

flatteningFailsProduces.question: What if flattening fails or produces errors?
flatteningFailsProduces.answer: A small number of PDFs use exotic field appearance streams that the flattening engine can't process; in that case you get a clear error and your file is left unchanged. Password-protected files must be unlocked first, and corrupted files should be repaired or re-exported before retrying.

scannedPdfs.question: Why is no text extracted from my scanned PDF?
scannedPdfs.answer: Scanned PDFs are images of pages and have no text layer, so there is no text to extract. That requires OCR (optical character recognition) — use our OCR PDF tool to add a searchable text layer (Arabic, English, and French supported), then extract the text here. This tool works with PDFs that contain real, selectable text.

copyText.question: How do I copy text from a PDF?
copyText.answer: Upload your PDF, wait a moment while the text is extracted, then click "Copy to clipboard". You can also download everything as a .txt file, or select just a part of the preview and copy it.

formatting.question: Will the layout and formatting be preserved?
formatting.answer: You get plain text: paragraphs and line breaks are kept as well as possible, but fonts, colors, columns and tables are not preserved. For editable formatting, try our PDF to Word tool.

free.question: Is this PDF to text converter free?
free.answer: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up and no watermarks. Files up to 50MB are supported, and since everything runs in your browser there is nothing to wait for on a server.

extractTextPdf.question: How to extract text from a PDF online
extractTextPdf.answer: Upload your PDF and the text is extracted automatically, page by page, directly in your browser. A live preview shows the result with character and word counts. Click "Copy to clipboard" or "Download as .txt" to save the text. Nothing is uploaded to a server.

copyTextInstead.question: Can I copy the text instead of downloading it?
copyTextInstead.answer: Yes. After extraction, click "Copy to clipboard" to copy the full text at once, or select just a portion of the preview and copy it manually. You can also download everything as a .txt file named after your PDF.

extractArabicText.question: Does it extract Arabic text?
extractArabicText.answer: Yes, Arabic text is extracted when the PDF contains a proper Unicode text layer, and the preview automatically switches to right-to-left display. Some Arabic PDFs store text in non-standard ways, so results can vary; scanned Arabic documents should go through the OCR tool first.

pageSeparators.question: What are the page separators?
pageSeparators.answer: The "Insert page separators" option adds a "--- Page N ---" marker between pages in the output, so you can tell where each page starts. Untick the checkbox to get one continuous text without markers. The preview updates instantly either way.

fileSizeLimits.question: What are the file size limits?
fileSizeLimits.answer: You can load PDF files up to 50MB. There is no page limit — a progress bar shows extraction advancing page by page. Because processing is local, large files depend on your device's speed rather than on any server.

textExtraction.question: How long does text extraction take?
textExtraction.answer: Most PDFs are done in a few seconds. Since everything runs in your browser, speed depends on your device and the document's size and complexity — there is no upload or download wait, and no server queue.

originalFileModified.question: Is my original file modified?
originalFileModified.answer: No. The tool only reads your PDF to extract its text; the file itself is never changed. The extracted text is saved as a separate .txt file, and your original PDF stays exactly as it was on your device.

extractTextPassword.question: Can I extract text from password-protected PDFs?
extractTextPassword.answer: Not directly. Encrypted PDFs cannot be opened without the password, so the tool will show a hint instead of a result. Remove the password first with the BlendPDF Unlock PDF tool, then extract the text.

extractTextMobile.question: Can I extract text on mobile devices?
extractTextMobile.answer: Yes, the tool works on smartphones and tablets. Extraction runs locally in your mobile browser, and you can copy the text to your clipboard or download the .txt file just like on desktop.

fileExtraction.question: What happens to my file after extraction?
fileExtraction.answer: Nothing is uploaded, so there is nothing to delete server-side. Your PDF is read locally in your browser's memory and released when you close or reload the page. The file and the extracted text stay entirely on your device.

extractionFailsText.question: What if extraction fails or the text looks wrong?
extractionFailsText.answer: Common causes are scanned PDFs without a text layer (use the OCR tool), password protection (unlock first), corrupted files, or the 50MB limit. Odd word order or spacing usually reflects how text is stored inside the PDF. Refresh the page and try again if extraction fails unexpectedly.

formats.question: What presentation formats are supported?
formats.answer: We support Microsoft PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx) and OpenDocument Presentation (.odp) files. Each slide in your presentation becomes one page in the PDF.

quality.question: Will my slides look the same in the PDF?
quality.answer: Slides keep their layout, images, charts, and text positioning as closely as possible. Presentations that use uncommon fonts may see minor font substitutions — embedding fonts in your PowerPoint file gives the closest match.

animations.question: What happens to animations and transitions?
animations.answer: PDF is a static format, so animations, transitions, and embedded video or audio are not carried over. Each slide is captured in its final state — build steps appear fully revealed.

fileSize.question: What are the file size limits?
fileSize.answer: You can convert presentations up to 50MB in size. There's no limit on the number of slides, but larger files may take longer to process.

privacy.question: Is my presentation secure?
privacy.answer: Yes. Your files are processed securely and never stored — Files are deleted from our servers within 1 hour — most immediately after processing. We never read or share your presentations.

cost.question: Is this really free?
cost.answer: Yes, completely free! No sign-up, no credit card, no hidden fees. Convert as many PowerPoint presentations to PDF as you need.

convertPowerpointPdf.question: How to convert PowerPoint to PDF online
convertPowerpointPdf.answer: Upload your presentation (.ppt, .pptx, or .odp) by dragging it onto the upload area or clicking "Select File", then click the convert button. The conversion runs on our servers and your PDF downloads in seconds, with each slide becoming one PDF page.

fontsHandledConversion.question: How are fonts handled during conversion?
fontsHandledConversion.answer: Common fonts convert with high fidelity. If your presentation uses an uncommon font that is not available on the conversion server, a visually similar font is substituted. Embedding fonts in your PowerPoint file before uploading gives the closest match.

slidesMapPdf.question: How do slides map to PDF pages?
slidesMapPdf.answer: Each slide becomes exactly one PDF page, in the same order as the presentation. The page keeps the slide's aspect ratio, so widescreen 16:9 decks produce widescreen PDF pages.

conversion.question: How long does conversion take?
conversion.answer: Most presentations convert in a few seconds. Large, image-heavy decks can take longer, and total time also depends on your upload speed since the conversion happens on our servers.

uploadPresentationsGoogle.question: Can I upload presentations from Google Drive?
uploadPresentationsGoogle.answer: Yes, the upload area includes a Google Drive picker so you can select a PowerPoint file stored in your Drive without downloading it to your device first.

convertKeynoteGoogle.question: Can I convert Keynote or Google Slides presentations?
convertKeynoteGoogle.answer: Not directly, but both apps can export to PowerPoint format. In Google Slides use File > Download > Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx); in Keynote use File > Export To > PowerPoint. Then upload the exported .pptx to BlendPDF.

originalPresentationModified.question: Is my original presentation modified?
originalPresentationModified.answer: No, your original file is never modified. BlendPDF creates a brand-new PDF while your PowerPoint file stays untouched on your device or in your Google Drive.

convertPowerpointPdfMobile.question: Can I convert PowerPoint to PDF on mobile devices?
convertPowerpointPdfMobile.answer: Yes, BlendPDF works on smartphones and tablets. Because the conversion runs on our servers, even older phones can convert large presentations — only upload and download speed depend on your connection.

convertingPowerpointPdf.question: Is converting PowerPoint to PDF free?
convertingPowerpointPdf.answer: Yes, completely free — no sign-up, no credit card, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Convert as many presentations as you need.

filesConversion.question: What happens to my files after conversion?
filesConversion.answer: All uploaded files are automatically deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share the contents of your presentations. No permanent storage is maintained.

conversionFailsProduces.question: What if the conversion fails or produces errors?
conversionFailsProduces.answer: Common causes are files over 50MB, corrupted presentations, or unsupported formats. Verify the file opens correctly in PowerPoint or LibreOffice, check your connection, and retry. Error messages indicate the specific problem.

whatIsMetadata.question: What metadata does a PDF contain?
whatIsMetadata.answer: Most PDFs carry hidden fields you never see on the page: the author's name (often a real personal or company account name), title, subject, keywords, the software that created it, and creation and modification timestamps. Many also embed an XMP metadata stream with the same details in XML form.

whatIsRemoved.question: What exactly does this tool remove?
whatIsRemoved.answer: It clears the document information fields (title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer), deletes the creation and modification dates, and strips the embedded XMP metadata stream. It does not change the visible content of your pages, and it does not remove text, annotations or attachments inside the document.

inBrowser.question: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
inBrowser.answer: No. This tool runs 100% in your browser — your file never leaves your device. That matters here more than anywhere: you are cleaning a document for privacy, so it should not travel over the internet at all.

whyRemove.question: Why should I remove metadata before sharing a PDF?
whyRemove.answer: Metadata can quietly reveal who wrote a document, which software and account created it, and exactly when it was made or edited. Removing it before you share a CV, contract, report or public document prevents leaking names, timelines and internal tooling.

encrypted.question: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
encrypted.answer: Not directly — encrypted PDFs can't be modified without the password. Use our Unlock PDF tool to remove the password first, then clean the metadata here.

verifyMetadataGone.question: How can I verify the metadata is really gone?
verifyMetadataGone.answer: After cleaning, BlendPDF re-opens the cleaned file and reads its metadata back, showing a before/after table where each removed field is confirmed. You can also check the downloaded file yourself in any PDF viewer's document properties.

removingMetadataChange.question: Does removing metadata change the visible content?
removingMetadataChange.answer: No. Pages, text, images, and formatting stay exactly as they were — only the hidden document information fields and the XMP stream are removed. Annotations, attachments, and the text itself are not touched.

hiddenDataRemoved.question: What hidden data is NOT removed?
hiddenDataRemoved.answer: The tool removes document-level metadata only. It does not delete annotations, comments, attachments, bookmarks, form data, or sensitive text visible on the pages. If the content itself contains private information, you need to redact it separately.

xmpMetadataStream.question: What is the XMP metadata stream?
xmpMetadataStream.answer: XMP is an XML block embedded in many PDFs that duplicates and extends the basic metadata — author, software, timestamps, and sometimes document history. Deleting only the info fields leaves XMP behind, which is why this tool strips the whole XMP stream from the document catalog as well.

fileSizeLimits.question: What are the file size limits?
fileSizeLimits.answer: PDF files up to 50MB are supported, with no page limit. Since processing is local, speed depends on your device rather than a server, and metadata removal is fast even for large documents.

originalFileModified.question: Is my original file modified?
originalFileModified.answer: No. The cleaned PDF is saved as a new file prefixed with "no-metadata-", and your original stays untouched on your device. You keep both versions.

removeMetadataMobile.question: Can I remove metadata on mobile devices?
removeMetadataMobile.answer: Yes, the tool works on smartphones and tablets. The metadata table, removal button, and download all work in mobile browsers, and processing stays local to your device.

removingPdfMetadata.question: Is removing PDF metadata free?
removingPdfMetadata.answer: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Files up to 50MB are supported, and unlimited documents can be cleaned.

metadataRemovalFails.question: What if metadata removal fails?
metadataRemovalFails.answer: Common causes are password-protected files (unlock first), corrupted PDFs, or files over 50MB. Some malformed documents can't be re-saved by the cleaning engine. Verify the file opens in a PDF viewer, then try again; if a specific field resists removal, the before/after table will show it honestly.

whatIsOcr.question: What is OCR and what does this tool do?
whatIsOcr.answer: OCR (optical character recognition) turns pictures of text — like scanned pages or photographed documents — into real text a computer can read. This tool adds that recognized text as an invisible layer inside your PDF, so the file looks exactly the same but becomes searchable, selectable, and copyable.

arabic.question: How good is the Arabic OCR?
arabic.answer: Arabic is a first-class language here, not an afterthought — we use the Tesseract engine with its dedicated Arabic model, which handles connected script and right-to-left text properly. Accuracy is good but not perfect: it depends heavily on scan quality, so clean 300-DPI scans of printed text work far better than blurry photos or handwriting. For best results, scan straight, well-lit pages.

limits.question: What are the file limits?
limits.answer: Files can be up to 50MB and 50 pages. OCR is genuinely slow — expect roughly 1–2 seconds per page — so larger documents would time out. If your file is bigger, split it with our Split PDF tool and OCR the parts separately, or compress it first.

alreadyHasText.question: Why does it say my PDF already has text?
alreadyHasText.answer: If every page already contains a text layer (for example, a PDF exported from Word), there is nothing for OCR to add, so we tell you instead of silently returning the same file. If the existing text is wrong or garbled, enable "Re-OCR pages that already have text" to replace it with freshly recognized text.

privacy.question: Is my document safe?
privacy.answer: OCR runs on our server, since text recognition is too heavy to do in your browser. Your file is processed in temporary storage and automatically deleted within 1 hour — we never read, share, or keep your documents.

pdfToWord.question: Can I turn the scanned PDF into a Word document?
pdfToWord.answer: Yes — a great workflow is to OCR the scan here first, then run the searchable result through our PDF to Word tool. Without the OCR step, a scanned PDF converts to Word as images; with it, you get editable text.

scannedPdfSearchable.question: How to make a scanned PDF searchable
scannedPdfSearchable.answer: Upload your scanned PDF, tick the recognition languages it contains (Arabic, English, or French), and click the OCR button. Processing takes roughly 1-2 seconds per page, then the searchable PDF downloads with an invisible text layer added over each scan.

whichLanguagesSupported.question: Which languages are supported?
whichLanguagesSupported.answer: Three languages are supported: Arabic, English, and French. You can select any combination for mixed-language documents, such as Arabic contracts with English clauses. At least one language must be selected before running OCR.

ocrChangePdf.question: Does OCR change how my PDF looks?
ocrChangePdf.answer: No. The recognized text is placed as an invisible layer exactly on top of the original scan, so the document looks identical — stamps, signatures, and layout untouched — but becomes searchable and copyable.

fileSizePage.question: What are the file size and page limits?
fileSizePage.answer: Files can be up to 50MB and 50 pages. OCR is computationally heavy — roughly 1-2 seconds per page — so larger documents would time out. Split bigger files with the Split PDF tool and OCR the parts separately, or compress oversized files first.

ocr.question: How long does OCR take?
ocr.answer: Expect roughly 1-2 seconds per page, so a 30-page scan can take about a minute. OCR jobs run one at a time on the server; at busy moments you may be asked to retry in a minute.

accurateOcr.question: How accurate is the OCR?
accurateOcr.answer: Accuracy is good but never perfect, and depends heavily on scan quality. Clean, straight, well-lit 300-DPI scans of printed text give excellent results; blurry photos, skewed pages, and low-resolution scans reduce accuracy in any OCR system.

ocrReadHandwriting.question: Can OCR read handwriting?
ocrReadHandwriting.answer: Not reliably. The recognition engine is designed for printed, typeset text. Neat block capitals may partially recognize, but cursive handwriting — in any language — generally will not. Handwritten notes and signatures stay visible in the PDF; they just will not become searchable text.

ocrPasswordProtected.question: Can I OCR a password-protected PDF?
ocrPasswordProtected.answer: No, encrypted PDFs are rejected with a clear message. Remove the password first with the Unlock PDF tool, run OCR on the unlocked file, then re-protect the result if needed.

ocrFree.question: Is OCR free?
ocrFree.answer: Yes, completely free — no sign-up, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Because OCR is the heaviest tool on our servers, usage is limited to 5 documents per 15 minutes, which covers normal use comfortably.

filesOcr.question: What happens to my files after OCR?
filesOcr.answer: All uploaded files are automatically deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share the contents of your documents. No permanent storage is maintained.

ocrFailsProduces.question: What if OCR fails or produces errors?
ocrFailsProduces.answer: The tool reports specific problems: files over 50MB or 50 pages, password-protected PDFs, pages that already have text, or a busy server. Each message says what to do — split, unlock, enable re-OCR, or retry in a minute.
